The *Muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text located in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the biographical past-life deed and karmic fruits of the elder (thera) Muṭṭhipupphiya [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages, though it identifies no external parallels in non-Pali canonical collections [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse data computed by DharmaNexus shows substantial Pali-internal reuse, with 38 matching passages identified across 10 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most extensive overlap occurs with the commentary on the Theragāthā (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), comprising 17 matches and 1,525 shared characters, including a continuous alignment covering segments §0.3–5.3 [DharmaNexus]. The remaining internal matches reflect standard formulaic verse material—particularly concentrated around verses §4.4–7.1—shared with various other poems in the Therāpadāna, including the *Pupphacchattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 331), *Ekacāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 191), and *Tikaṇṇipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 190) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan meeting the match threshold [DharmaNexus].
